# Council A, round 3: the v22 probe is back; a recommendation to agree or reject (read-only; do not edit files or run model calls)

The probe of `clean-arch/step2-revision-links-2026-11-10/PROBE-v22.md` was sent after one more sender review
(`council/probe-review-codex.md`; its one serious finding, the reader not bound to its case, was closed and shown). Six of six
answered, $0.0109. Raw answers and reading: `poc/data/clean-step2-revision-links-2026-11-10/judge-probe-v22/`.

| v22, FY2028 total revenue, draw 3, 2026-07-06 | Rungs | Implied revenue | The four delay reports and NVIDIA's answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| As saved (the carried answer shown) | 2, 2, 2 | about $553, $553–554, $554 billion | all three reasons set the answer against the reports ("countervailing, though not a quantified rebuttal"; "Nvidia says its roadmap is intact"; "counters the delay reports") |
| The carried answer not shown | 2, **3**, 2 | "low $550s", **about $545**, $553–554 billion | the reports stand alone; one answer "would shade that forecast below the $550 billion boundary" |

By the rule fixed beforehand: not decided (mixed). The first probe (draw 1, the same statement carried into FY2027 Blackwell and
Rubin revenue, which both reader families now call context): 2, 2, 2 against 2, 2, 2, and no reason used the statement.

My reading (challenge it):
1. Two traced links, opposite in kind. Where the readers call the carried link context, removing it changed nothing and the reasons
   never used it. Where the readers call it evidence, the reasons used it three times of three and, without it, one answer of three
   crossed a rung boundary that none crossed with it. Neither is proof; both point the same way: the carried links that matter to a
   conclusion are the ones worth keeping.
2. So "never carry" removes 19 links that do not seem to move conclusions and 3 to 5 that readers would keep, one of which the
   judge leaned on. On what is measured, that is a worse trade than leaving the rule as it is. I withdraw the suggestion I gave
   Alex on draw 1 alone.
3. There is no rule a program can apply that keeps the 3 and drops the 19 (round 2, agreed). The owner of the real defect is
   upstream: Step 1 filed four reports under a question and did not file the company's answer there (a link miss on a contrary
   fact, the class already open as defect 3 of `docs/CURRENT_STATE.md`, "Link clutter", whose protected link check Alex approved
   designing); and Jev's choice of target among the statements of one story.

Proposed recommendation to Alex (one recommendation, one test):
- **Recommendation: do not change the rule. The writer keeps carrying.** Record why, with the counts; keep the clutter as a recorded
  defect of about 1% of what the judge reads; name Step 1's linking as the owner of "a company's answer is filed where the report
  it answers is filed", without starting that work.
- **The test, only if Alex wants the choice settled on the whole class rather than on two cases:** every one of the 24 carried
  links, the question's judgement on the link's day as saved and without that one link, three answers each: 144 calls, about $0.30
  at the rates the two probes cost, each case built by the replay that built these two. Read per link by the same rule, and
  reported by the readers' class (19 context, 3 evidence, 2 split). It would show how many context links move a conclusion (the
  cost of carrying) and how many evidence links do (its benefit). It still would not cover later days or the four question-days
  judged only for a carried link.
- I would tell him plainly that this is a small matter either way and that I do not think the test is worth his next slot; Step 4
  is where nothing is yet shown.

Questions:
- (a) Do you agree with "do not change the rule", or does the evidence still support "never carry" or a third option? Name the
  strongest reason against my recommendation.
- (b) Is the 144-call test the right single test if he wants one, or is there a cheaper decisive one?
- (c) Any claim above that the files do not support?
Under 450 words.
